reason: E1 confirms the initial homogeneous solid-solution state in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles. E2 demonstrates that entropy-stabilized structures have sluggish diffusion kinetics which maintain uniform elemental distribution during annealing, and that full diffusion equilibration leads to segregation. However, neither cited passage provides evidence linking segregation to degraded catalytic or thermoelectric performance, leaving that premise unsupported.
premises: CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles can be synthesized as a homogeneous solid solution with random elemental distribution.
High-entropy alloy nanoparticles exhibit sluggish diffusion kinetics due to high diffusion barriers.
Sluggish diffusion kinetics can kinetically limit atomic diffusion and prevent elemental segregation during thermal annealing.
When diffusion is thermally activated and overcomes kinetic barriers, elemental segregation and phase instabilities occur.
Elemental segregation leads to degradation of catalytic and thermoelectric performance.
